You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Alternate location is Toulouse, France.

**Our Benefits for You**

  • **Fair Compensation & Extras:** Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.
  • **Time for You (and Your Loved Ones):** 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement; work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.
  • **Growth Made Easy:** Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.
  • **Feel Good at Work:** On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.
  • **Diversity Connects:** Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

**Your tasks and responsibilities**

  • Drive the E2E PLM Portfolio roadmap as an Enterprise/Functional Architect to define IS convergence strategies for Large Solutions.
  • Design and communicate a shared technical vision while building the Architectural Runway to sustain long-term business value.
  • Partner with Solution Train Engineers and Product Management to steer the operational delivery of the Large Solution.
  • Coordinate across multiple Agile Release Trains (ARTs) to ensure seamless System Integration and technical alignment.
  • Lead architecture boards and facilitate key SAFe ceremonies, including PI Planning, to govern technical standards.
  • Secure project milestones by providing deep functional expertise and contributing to strategic roadmap definitions.
  • Manage supplier team performance, providing the leadership and monitoring necessary to scale architectural activities.

**Desired skills and qualifications**

  • Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • At least 8 years of experience in Business IT projects, with proven expertise in Software Architecture and Development.
  • Solid background in PLM, Digital, Flight Test, and/or Avionics domains.
  • Strong knowledge of Design, Engineering, and Digital Processes.
  • Strong leadership, conflict resolution, and cross-functional stakeholder management skills to align business partners across complex environments.
  • Outstanding communication skills with a proven ability to convey complex technical architectures to diverse audiences.
  • Advanced level of English and French.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.

Take your career to a new level and apply online **now in English**, mentioning your **salary expectations and earliest starting date!**

title: Vice President, Health Information and Technology
description:
Texas Health Action (THA) is a community-informed non-profit organization dedicated to providing access to culturally affirming, quality health services in a safe and supportive environment, with expertise in serving LGBTQIA+ people and those impacted by HIV. Kind Clinic proudly serves Texas with four vibrant locations: two in Austin, one in San Antonio, and another in Dallas plus virtual care services available to all residents across Texas. The Vice President, Health Information & Technology provides senior level leadership for the organization’s Information Technology (IT) and Health Information Management (HIM) functions, including clinical applications, data systems, interoperability, security, and information/data governance. This role is responsible for the technology and information system infrastructure of the organization and its future direction.

This role serves as a strategic partner to the CEO, translating organizational goals into a cohesive technology and data strategy and ensuring disciplined execution across infrastructure, clinical systems, analytics, and compliance. The VP is accountable for aligning technology investments with patient care and experience, operational excellence, regulatory requirements, and long-term organizational growth.

Core Functions

title: Transformer Shop Refurbishment Technician
description:
Transformer Shop Refurbishment Technician

Location: Tampa, FL
Pay: $35–$45 per hour
Employment Type: Direct Hire Opportunity

Superior Skilled Trades is partnered with a company seeking an experienced Transformer Shop Refurbishment Technician to join their team in Tampa, FL. This position is responsible for the hands-on refurbishment, repair, reassembly, and testing of small and medium substation and transmission-class power transformers in a controlled shop environment.

The ideal candidate has practical experience working with power transformers and understands transformer components, electrical testing, mechanical assembly, troubleshooting, and safe work practices. This role works closely with engineering, testing personnel, quality, and shop leadership to ensure refurbished transformers meet applicable specifications and are ready for service.

Responsibilities

  • Inspect incoming transformers and document nameplate information, condition, damage, and missing components.
  • Disassemble single-phase and three-phase transformers for inspection and refurbishment.
  • Inspect cores, windings, insulation, leads, bushings, connections, tanks, and other transformer components for damage, wear, contamination, or defects.
  • Repair or replace damaged electrical and mechanical components according to approved procedures.
  • Clean and treat transformer cores, coils, tanks, and other components using appropriate processes and materials.
  • Maintain proper cleanliness and moisture control when working with exposed transformer components.
  • Reassemble cores, coils, leads, bushings, connections, and hardware using drawings, specifications, and approved procedures.
  • Properly identify and document lead locations, polarity, tap positions, hardware, and component information during disassembly and reassembly.
  • Assist with transformer oil processing, sampling, purification, filling, and leak checks as required.
  • Perform electrical and mechanical testing on refurbished transformers.
  • Set up and perform assigned transformer tests, which may include turns ratio, polarity, winding resistance, insulation resistance, excitation current, and other diagnostic tests.
  • Review test results, identify abnormal readings, and troubleshoot potential electrical or mechanical problems.
  • Verify test equipment, connections, transformer identification, and test procedures before testing.
  • Escalate test results or repair conditions that require engineering or senior technical review.
  • Maintain accurate refurbishment reports, test logs, photographs, repair records, and inspection documentation.
  • Prepare completed transformers for painting, labeling, final inspection, and shipment.
  • Operate hand tools, power tools, lifting equipment, forklifts, and overhead cranes safely.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, including de-energization, electrical safety, material handling, chemical handling, and shop housekeeping requirements.
  • Work with engineering and shop leadership to resolve defects, non-conformances, and issues identified during refurbishment or testing.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Trade school, technical certificate, or electrical training preferred.
  • 1–3+ years of hands-on experience working with electrical transformers, transformer refurbishment, transformer assembly, or related power equipment.
  • Working knowledge of transformer components, construction, wiring diagrams, and electrical testing methods.
  • Ability to read transformer nameplates, drawings, wiring diagrams, and test specifications.
  • Experience using electrical test instruments and interpreting test results.
  • Understanding of transformer diagnostic testing, including turns ratio, winding resistance, insulation resistance, polarity, and excitation current.
  • Ability to troubleshoot electrical and mechanical faults.
  • Experience with insulating oil handling, processing, or transformer oil systems is preferred.
  • Familiarity with vacuum drying, oil purification, tank repair, or transformer leak testing is a plus.
  • Forklift and/or overhead crane experience preferred.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, lifting equipment, and electrical test instruments.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately document work and test results.
  • Ability to work safely around electrical equipment, insulating oils, chemicals, and heavy transformer components.

Preferred Technical Knowledge

  • Power transformer construction and refurbishment
  • Transformer cores and windings
  • Bushings and connections
  • Tap changers and tap positions
  • Transformer oil processing and filling
  • Vacuum drying and moisture control
  • Turns ratio testing
  • Winding resistance testing
  • Insulation resistance testing
  • Excitation current testing
  • Polarity testing
  • Electrical and mechanical troubleshooting
  • ANSI/IEEE/NETA standards and testing practices
  • Transformer assembly and reassembly procedures
  • Torque requirements and mechanical connections
  • Forklift and overhead crane operation

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be a hands-on transformer technician, not simply someone with general electrical experience. The ideal candidate can explain how they have personally disassembled, inspected, repaired, reassembled, and tested transformers or comparable high-voltage electrical equipment.

Strong candidates should be comfortable identifying defects, following drawings and procedures, taking accurate measurements, troubleshooting abnormal test results, and documenting their work. They should also know when an issue requires escalation to engineering or shop leadership rather than making an unauthorized repair or technical decision.

Work Environment

  • Controlled transformer shop environment
  • Hands-on work with large electrical equipment and transformer components
  • Frequent use of hand tools, electrical test equipment, lifting equipment, forklifts, and/or overhead cranes
  • Exposure to insulating oils, cleaning chemicals, and industrial shop conditions
  • Requires strong attention to safety, cleanliness, documentation, and quality throughout the refurbishment process

title: Clinical Psychologist
description:
***$10,000 Sign On/Retention Bonus***
Your new company
GuideStar Eldercare’s mission is to enhance the quality of life for our shared patients by easing their suffering while actively promoting their safety, functionality, and dignity. Led by CEO/Founder, Dr. Steven Posar, our innovative care does not end with patient diagnosis and treatment. We work with long-term care facilities on complex psychological and medical management issues and regulatory compliance that help facilities establish and maintain high standards of care and compliance. Recognized as the only national LTC Behavioral Health Age-Friendly Health System, GuideStar has engaged in presenting innovative research at the Alzheimer's Association International Conferences.
Your new role
As a Clinical Psychologist with GuideStar Eldercare, you will join in our efforts to provide neuro-behavioral health services to residents in long term care facilities. Using a multi-disciplinary approach, you will partner with specialty clinicians to provide holistic, continuity of care for the elderly afflicted with neurocognitive disorders like dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, and other neurologic and/or psychiatric diagnoses.
What you'll do
- Provide evaluation
- Establish different diagnosis, i.e., Alzheimer's vs. Parkinson's vs. Vascular
- Provide cognitive assessments
- Provide condition-specific support therapy or when indicated, insight-based therapy
- Coordinate the patient's care plan with the facility, PCP and GuideStar colleagues, and engage with the family as indicated.
What you'll need to succeed
An active state Psychologist license, passion for the geriatric population, interest in neurobehavioral science, and a desire to make a difference in a population struggling with Alzheimer’s disease, dementia, and other neurodegenerative disorders. An HSPP is preferred in applicable states.
What you'll get in return
A full suite of benefits, including medical at 30 hours/week (company-paid premiums for eligible employees), dental, vision, life, long/short-term disability, 401K, licensing reimbursement (including license renewals), CEU reimbursement, in-house CEU offerings, 60-day new hire training program.
All GuideStar employees must be vaccinated against the flu. GuideStar follows all applicable laws; contact humanresources@guidestareldercare.com for more information. Testing for illegal drugs will be administered to all final candidates for whom an offer of employment has been extended.
How to Apply
If you are interested in working with the geriatric population, have a passion for neurobehavioral science, and a desire to make a difference in a population struggling with dementia and other neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders, click on the “apply now” button to forward your resume or contact us at careers@guidestareldercare.com for more information.

WHAT MAKES US GREAT
GuideStar Eldercare is the national leader in neurobehavioral long-term care services, providing expert neuropsychiatric and dementia care services to nursing homes and memory care facilities. GuideStar Eldercare's mission is to enhance the quality of life for patients by easing their suffering while actively promoting their safety, functionality, and dignity.

We believe in bringing the highest level of clinical care to the long-term care population. GuideStar is led by CEO and Founder Dr. Steven L. Posar, alongside our clinical team of expert physicians, psychiatrists, gerontologists, neurologists, and psychologists, who work with our clinical staff to find the best possible outcomes for our shared patients. Our neurologically based model ensures proper diagnosis and treatment, which improves care outcomes for patients with dementia, neurocognitive impairments, and/or psychiatric conditions.

GuideStar is dedicated to rigorous clinical care protocols and exceptional documentation and communication, based on the most up-to-date research and practice. Our dedication is underscored by our own research and desire to educate the greater long-term care industry. Most recently, our research on antipsychotic reduction through neurologic protocols was published in JAMDA in September of 2023. Associations and publications our research has been featured in include: PALTC, McKnight’s, AAGP, OHCA, and AAIC.

title: Staff Engineer, STPG PE NAND
company: MICRON SEMICONDUCTOR ASIA OPERATIONS PTE. LTD.
description:
Every gigabyte Micron ship is trusted to hold someone's data for years, whether in a phone, a car, a data center or an AI cluster. The NAND Product Reliability Architecture (NRA) team defines how we prove that trust before a product is released.

As a Staff Engineer in NAND Product Reliability Architecture team, you will own the reliability architecture for Micron's newest NAND products end-to-end: interpreting reliability requirements, architecting qualification and stress strategies, developing and integrating reliability algorithms and system features, and optimizing coverage, sampling and test time so that we qualify faster without compromising quality.

This is a high-leverage, high-visibility role. Your architecture decisions directly influence qualification cycle time, product time to market and the reliability our customers experience in the field. In a market where being first to qualify is a competitive advantage, speed is a core expectation. You will work closely with Technology Development, System Architecture, Design Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, and you will be expected to influence across these teams.

Main Responsibilities:

  • Comprehend NAND reliability specifications (internal, JEDEC, and customer-specific) to ensure complete coverage in the qualification plan.

  • Architect end-to-end reliability qualification strategies for new products and technology generations, including stress conditions, coverage models, sampling plans, readout points and acceptance criteria.

  • Benchmark specifications across product generations and application segments, identify gaps or unintended scope changes, and drive alignment with System and Quality teams.

  • Optimize qualification sampling and flow coverage to reduce cost and test time while preserving statistical confidence and customer protection.

  • Design and release reliability test flows across wafer-level and component-level platforms, ensuring readiness for new product and technology development programs.

  • Own and maintain clear reliability documentation and governance so test methods, stress conditions and supporting capabilities remain accurate, auditable and current.

  • Identify and validate test-time reduction opportunities, quantify their value and demonstrate them with data before production deployment.

  • Partner with execution and operations teams to ensure clean implementation and on-time, or accelerated, qualification release.

  • Define the architecture and integration strategy for new reliability algorithms, system features and product capabilities.

  • Drive system feature development in partnership with System Architecture, Design and Firmware teams by translating system-level requirements into component-level capability, defining validation criteria and confirming feature effectiveness before qualification use.

  • Develop, validate and deploy reliability-focused test capabilities; support emulation, bench checkout, debugging and issue resolution with Design and Test Engineering teams.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Own technical execution from concept through validation, product introduction and sustaining support.

  • Lead investigation of reliability failures and qualification gating issues using structured problem solving, electrical characterization and physical failure analysis.

  • Connect product-level failure signatures to device, process, circuit, firmware or system behavior and translate findings into actionable mitigations.

  • Provide data-backed reliability positions for product changes, process changes, manufacturing excursions and customer-specific requirements.

  • Support customer inquiries and communicate technical findings, risk assessments and recommendations clearly to engineering and leadership stakeholders.

  • Analyze large, high-dimensional reliability datasets, including threshold-voltage movement, error-rate trends, charge loss, read-disturb behavior and ECC margin, and convert the results into decision-ready recommendations.

  • Build and deploy automation and agentic AI workflows that reduce manual effort in flow generation, documentation, sampling design, data analysis and technical reporting.

  • Champion responsible, standards-compliant use of AI tools and share reusable solutions across the reliability organization.

  • Act as the recognized technical owner for an assigned product or reliability domain and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.

  • Mentor engineers, strengthen technical depth and establish sustainable backup ownership for critical reliability workflows.

  • Represent Product Reliability in architecture reviews, qualification reviews, technical working groups and leadership updates.

  • Drive innovation through new methodologies, technical publications, invention disclosures and continuous improvement of next-generation reliability capability.

AI Responsibilities

Minimum Required Qualifications/Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in semiconductor reliability, product engineering, test, design, validation, or system media architecture domain.

  • Solid understanding of non-volatile memory architecture and operation, including program, erase and read algorithms, threshold-voltage distributions, page and block structure and error-management concepts.

  • Hands-on experience in semiconductor reliability, product engineering, test, design, validation, firmware, system development or a closely related domain.

  • Experience in system feature development, including defining, developing, checking out and validating reliability-impacting features or algorithms, with an understanding of how controller, firmware and system-level behavior translate into component-level requirements.

  • Demonstrated architecture development capability, including strategy definition, coverage modeling, sampling design and trade-off analysis across quality, risk, cost and cycle time.

  • Working knowledge of semiconductor device physics, circuits, process technology and reliability failure mechanisms such as charge loss or gain, read disturb, retention, cycling degradation and oxide breakdown.

  • Strong statistical and data-analysis capability, with hands-on proficiency in Python, JMP, Tableau or equivalent tools.

  • Familiarity with applicable industry reliability standards and qualification sampling or confidence methodologies.

  • Demonstrated bias for speed, including a track record of accelerating schedules, pulling in milestones or simplifying processes without compromising quality, and comfort making sound decisions with incomplete data.

  • Excellent problem-solving, project-management and cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical positions clearly to both engineers and executives.

Highly Desirable/Preferred skills or experience

  • Direct experience with NAND component or wafer-level reliability testing, qualification-flow development or electrical failure analysis.

  • Experience owning a system feature or architecture from concept through production release and post-release sustaining.

  • Background in design-for-test, media or system architecture, controller development, firmware integration, silicon validation or advanced test development.

  • Experience with structured problem-solving methods such as 8D or FMEA.

title: Senior Software Engineer I
description:
About us:

Jeppesen ForeFlight is the industry leader in aviation software and data, serving commercial airlines, military operators, business aviation, and general aviation pilots worldwide. We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer I based in Singapore.

One third of pilots and cabin crew worldwide are flying with schedules produced by Jeppesen ForeFlight innovative solutions. One million pilots use our navigation products, and every day some 70,000 routes around the world are planned with the help of Jeppesen ForeFlight.

At Jeppesen Foreflight, you will work with breakthrough technology, exciting customers and fantastic colleagues from around the world. To get the best out of each talent, we encourage and enable our employees to continuously develop and explore. We are focusing on continuous improvements and innovations to bring more value to our clients in the future.

You are passionate about using technology to solve our clients’ real-world problems and improve their efficiency – you want to deliver solutions that our clients truly benefit from! Problem solving gets you excited, especially with others in a team working tightly with the client.

Collaboration and communication are your strengths. You find working with people from around the world to be exciting and stimulating.

You are flexible, thrive in a dynamic environment, and see change as something positive.

The Professional Services department is responsible for the configuration and delivery of our Crew and Ops management products to airline customers and to make sure that we deliver solutions that our customers truly need.   • MSc or BSc in Computer Science / Physics Engineering /Industrial Engineering or equivalent programing experience
  • Experienced with Unix / Linux environment
  • Strong team player qualities
  • Demonstrates strong communication skills in the English language

Preferred Qualifications / Competencies (Desired):

  • Python, Shell scripting, SQL, Web development, Java, functional programming

  • Ability to speak additional languages fluently

Typical Education & Experience

  • Education/experience typically acquired through MSc or BSc in Computer Science / Physics Engineering /Industrial Engineering or equivalent Programing experience

We put great emphasis on your personal characteristics. We value individuals who have an analytical approach to problem solving, strong communication skills both within and outside your team, an interest in technology as well as human relations and a curiosity to learn and explore new ways of doing things.

We are looking for both junior and senior candidates.

Relocation is not offered with this role.

At Jeppesen ForeFlight, we know you want a rewarding career. To do that, you need challenging projects, a good work environment, and awesome coworkers. Singapore

title: Technical Specialist
description:
Role Purpose

Sunollo is a fast-growing residential solar company in Singapore. We are looking for a Technical Specialist with an electrical engineering background to provide desk-based technical assurance across our solar projects.

The role is responsible for ensuring that project designs, electrical documentation and approval submissions are complete, technically correct and first-time right before they move to installation or regulatory submission.

The Technical Specialist will also provide technical support for electrical faults and customer issues across both ongoing and completed solar projects.

Key Ownership Areas

1. Project Technical Review & Design Validation

  • Review approximately 40–60 projects per month before they are released to installation partners.

  • Check Single-Line Diagrams, electrical drawings, rooftop panel layouts and related project documentation.

  • Validate system configuration, including panel layout, inverter selection, battery configuration and electrical connections.

  • Review relevant electrical calculations, including voltage, current and system capacity.

  • Identify technical errors, inconsistencies or missing information and coordinate corrections before project handover.

  • Ensure installers receive a complete and technically accurate project package.

Success looks like: Projects are installation-ready, technically correct and released with minimal downstream clarification, rework or design changes.

2. Permitting & LEW Submission Readiness

  • Prepare and review technical documentation required for solar permitting and approval processes.

  • Coordinate with Licensed Electrical Workers (LEWs) for regulatory submissions.

  • Check that submission packages contain complete and accurate information, including electrical drawings, SLDs, system details, meter information, photographs and supporting documentation.

  • Identify missing or incorrect information before submission and coordinate with Sales, Operations or other teams to close gaps.

  • Support technical clarification requests arising during the approval process.

  • Develop a working understanding of Singapore solar approval requirements and interactions with relevant authorities.

Success looks like: High first-time-right submission quality, fewer rejected or incomplete submissions, and reduced permitting delays caused by documentation errors.

3. Electrical Troubleshooting & Customer Support

  • Act as the technical point of contact for electrical issues escalated by Customer Experience, Operations, Maintenance or Installation teams.

  • Review drawings and system configurations to diagnose potential causes of faults or performance issues.

  • Support Project Managers, maintenance engineers and installers with electrical troubleshooting during installation, commissioning or after system activation.

  • Provide technical guidance on panels, inverters, batteries, wiring, cabling and electrical connections.

  • Explain technical issues and proposed solutions clearly to customers when required.

  • Track allocated technical cases through to satisfactory closure.

Success looks like: Technical issues are diagnosed accurately, resolved within agreed timelines, and communicated clearly to both internal teams and customers.

4. Process Excellence & First-Time-Right Delivery

  • Continually improve the quality of project documentation provided to installers and LEWs.

  • Develop and maintain technical checklists and validation standards.

  • Identify recurring documentation, design or submission errors and eliminate their root causes.

  • Work across Sales, Operations, Customer Experience, Maintenance and installation partners to improve information flow.

  • Standardise project documentation and review processes as Sunollo scales.

  • Track common technical errors and recommend improvements to systems, templates and workflows.

Success looks like: A progressively more reliable process with fewer errors, fewer handbacks, less rework and faster movement from sale to approval and installation.

Candidate Profile

Education

Diploma or Degree in:

  • Electrical Engineering

  • Electrical & Electronic Engineering

  • Power Engineering

  • Renewable Energy

  • Solar Energy

  • Or another relevant engineering discipline

Experience

  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant electrical engineering experience.

  • Experience in construction, engineering projects, M&E, electrical contracting, solar EPC or renewable energy environments.

  • Experience working with electrical drawings and project documentation.

  • Solar experience is preferred but candidates with strong electrical project experience and an interest in renewable energy will also be considered.

Technical Skills

The successful candidate should be comfortable with:

  • Single-Line Diagrams

  • Electrical drawings and schematics

  • Current and voltage calculations

  • AC and DC electrical systems

  • Cable and wiring requirements

  • Electrical protection and connections

  • Solar PV panels

  • Inverters and hybrid inverters

  • Battery Energy Storage Systems

  • Rooftop solar layouts

  • Electrical troubleshooting

  • Technical documentation

  • Regulatory and approval documentation

Key Performance Measures

  • Percentage of projects released first-time right

  • Number of technical errors identified after installer handover

  • First-time-right rate for LEW submission packages

  • Reduction in approval delays caused by incomplete documentation

  • Turnaround time for project technical reviews

  • Resolution time for electrical support cases

  • Reduction in recurring design and documentation errors

  • Quality and consistency of project technical documentation

title: Staff Engineer, AI R&D
description:
Why Join dLocal?
dLocal is the financial infrastructure powering global commerce in the world's fastest-growing markets. The biggest companies in the world trust us to unlock growth in 60+ countries across emerging markets—moving money where others see complexity. We don't just process payments; we are architects of payment ecosystems and partners in our customers' expansion. You'll work alongside 1,300+ teammates from 40+ nationalities and tackle global challenges from day one.


What's the Opportunity?

As a Staff Engineer in AI R&D, you set the technical direction for agentic and LLM-based systems, raise the engineering bar of the teams around you, and take on the hardest design and production problems. You will join one of our AI R&D teams, matched to your profile and to the company's most pressing needs, and you will work across team boundaries whenever the problem requires it.

You will also take technical leadership of important initiatives: shaping the approach, guiding the team through execution from design to production, and keeping the work aligned with peers across engineering and with the business areas it serves. You will engage with those stakeholders directly, so that decisions are made quickly and with full context.

The areas where you could contribute include:

  • AI-native software delivery: agents that support the full software lifecycle, from planning and coding to review, testing and incident response.

  • Business process automation: a self-service platform where business areas configure and own agentic automations, with human review and full traceability.

  • AI platform foundations: shared services such as LLM access and routing, secure tool and system integrations, reusable agent components and governed skills and plugins.

Where you land is decided during the selection process, based on your experience, your interests and the needs of each team.

What Will I Be Doing?

Technical Leadership of Initiatives

  • Act as the technical lead of AI initiatives, from the first definition of the problem through delivery in production, working alongside the engineers and team leads who execute them.

  • Work directly with peers and business stakeholders to understand needs, agree on scope and priorities, and keep expectations aligned as the work evolves.

  • Translate business goals into technical plans, milestones and trade-offs, and raise risks early.

  • Make sure initiatives reach production with outcomes that can be measured and explained to the business.

Architecture & Technical Direction

  • Lead the design and architecture of AI systems, including agentic workflows, retrieval, tool use, orchestration and state management, built by one or several teams.

  • Define reference architectures, patterns and engineering standards that other teams adopt and reuse.

  • Make and document trade-off decisions across quality, latency, cost, security and vendor dependency.

  • Solve the most complex technical problems in your area and unblock the teams around you.

Quality & Evaluation of AI Systems

  • Establish how AI behavior is measured: evaluation datasets, regression tracking, quality metrics and acceptance criteria for agents and LLM-based features.

  • Ensure systems are tested against realistic cases, not only demos, before and after they reach production.

  • Define the telemetry needed to understand cost, latency, quality and outcomes end to end.

Production Excellence

  • Lead operational practices: reliability, scalability, resilience, observability and incident learning for AI services.

  • Examine production behavior, identify structural improvements and drive them to completion with the owning teams.

  • Keep cost under control through routing, caching, context management and capacity decisions.

Security, Governance & Compliance by Design

  • Design controlled access for agents that act on internal systems: permissions, guardrails, audit trails and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

  • Work with Security, Legal, Compliance and IT so that governance requirements are built into reusable components and not rebuilt for every use case.

Multiplying Impact

  • Mentor engineers and tech leads, and raise the technical level of the teams you work with.

  • Turn what you learn into playbooks, templates, shared libraries and documentation that others can use without you.

  • Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and align teams around shared standards.

  • Share knowledge through internal write-ups and tech talks, and occasionally through external meetups and conferences.

What Skills Do I Need?

Technical depth

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience operating at senior or Staff-level scope.

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience building and operating systems based on LLMs, ideally in production.

  • Experience designing agentic or multi-step AI systems involving tool use, orchestration, state, retrieval or external integrations.

  • Strong foundations in distributed systems, including synchronous and asynchronous communication, and in software architecture principles and practices.

  • Solid knowledge of cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS, and of running services securely and cost-consciously.

  • Experience with observability, testing and evaluation of complex systems.

Technical leadership

  • Track record of technically leading initiatives that involve multiple teams, from design to production.

  • Comfortable working directly with business stakeholders and engineering peers to agree on scope, priorities and outcomes.

  • Ability to understand trade-offs, make decisions with incomplete information and stay effective in crisis situations.

  • Experience defining engineering standards and best practices that teams actually adopt.

  • Able to influence without authority, and to explain technical decisions to non-specialists in concrete, concise terms.

Nice to have

  • Experience with agent frameworks and protocols such as LangChain, LangGraph, the Claude Agent SDK or MCP.

  • Experience with Kubernetes and containerized execution environments.

  • Experience with LLM gateways, model routing and cost management.

  • Background in machine learning or applied research.

  • Experience in regulated environments such as payments or financial services.

Mindset

  • Builder attitude: you prefer reusable platforms and tools over one-off solutions.

  • Curious and biased toward experimentation, combined with disciplined measurement and risk awareness.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-moving field, and able to structure your own work and keep stakeholders informed.

What do we offer?
Besides the tailored benefits we have for each country, dLocal will help you thrive and go that extra mile by offering you:
- Flexibility in how you work: We focus on impact and productivity over fixed hours. This means our teams have flexible schedules and, depending on your role and location, you will combine self‑managed focus time with moments of in‑person connection in our collaboration hubs.
- Fintech industry: work in a dynamic and ever-evolving environment, with plenty to build and boost your creativity.
- Referral bonus program: our internal talents are the best recruiters - refer someone ideal for a role and get rewarded.
- Work From Anywhere: Team members can work while traveling for up to 3 months every year.
What happens after you apply?
Our Talent Acquisition team is invested in creating the best candidate experience possible, so don’t worry, you will definitely hear from us. We will review your CV and keep you posted by email at every step of the process!
Also, you can check out our webpage, Linkedin and Youtube for more about dLocal!

title: Information Systems Security Officer
description:
SMS is seeking an Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) I to support the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) at Edwards Air Force Base. The ISSO I provides cybersecurity, Assessment and Authorization (A&A), and Risk Management Framework (RMF) support throughout the system lifecycle. The position develops and maintains security documentation, evaluates risk, supports security control testing and continuous monitoring, and works with system owners, administrators, cybersecurity personnel, assessors, and government stakeholders to support system authorization and maintain compliance with applicable DoD, Department of the Air Force, NIST, and DISA requirements.

Since 1976, SMS has specialized in modernizing legacy IT and sustaining complex enterprise environments for federal agencies. With the goal of building long-term partnerships with our customers, we invest in our employees by providing the training, tools, and support they need to keep critical missions operational, improve performance, and reduce risk. SMS is headquartered in McLean, Virginia, with offices and on-site operations at customer locations throughout the United States. For additional information on SMS, visit .

Submit your resume today!

Job Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain, and update System Security Plans (SSPs), risk assessments, Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and other RMF/A&A authorization artifacts.

  • Categorize information systems and support security-control selection using DoDI 8510.01, NIST SP 800-60, applicable RMF baselines, and the RMF IT Categorization and Selection Checklist (ITCSC).

  • Evaluate system risks and vulnerabilities using RMF methodology and recommend mitigation or remediation strategies.

  • Collaborate with system owners, system administrators, cybersecurity personnel, assessors, and other stakeholders throughout the A&A process.

  • Ensure security controls are incorporated into system design and operations; support testing, validation, and collection of evidence demonstrating control effectiveness.

  • Use vulnerability and compliance tools such as Nessus or SCAP to identify technical vulnerabilities, support remediation, and validate secure configurations.

  • Validate systems against applicable DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), document deviations, and coordinate corrective actions.

  • Establish and support continuous monitoring activities, maintain visibility of system security posture, and provide status to the ISSM and Authorizing Official (AO).

  • Maintain accurate documentation for system changes, secure configurations, cybersecurity incidents, threats, deficiencies, mitigations, and authorization decisions.

  • Support assessment teams by providing required documentation, evidence, and system access for security-control testing.

  • Verify systems meet applicable security criteria before AO review and support ATO/DTO risk decisions with clear summaries of system risk posture.

  • Provide DoD RMF and cybersecurity subject-matter support to technical teams, customers, and decision-makers.

  • Ensure required users and administrators complete System Rules of Behavior and Authorized Use Agreements in accordance with applicable Air Force, Space Force, and AFRL RMF guidance.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of cybersecurity, information assurance, information system security, or related experience, including experience supporting RMF activities.

  • Working knowledge of DoD RMF and A&A processes, including SSPs, POA&Ms, security controls, risk assessments, continuous monitoring, and authorization documentation.

  • Familiarity with DoDI 8510.01, NIST guidance, DISA STIGs, and applicable DoD cybersecurity requirements.

  • Experience supporting vulnerability assessment, security compliance, and remediation activities; familiarity with tools such as Nessus, SCAP, ACAS, or Tenable.

  • Technical understanding of enterprise infrastructure, Microsoft Windows, Linux, networking, and common cybersecurity technologies sufficient to support system security activities.

  • Strong documentation, analytical, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to coordinate across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret Security Clearance.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain applicable DoD 8140 workforce qualification requirements within the required timeframe.

  • Maintain an IAT level II certification.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience supporting DoD, Department of the Air Force, AFRL, classified, research, laboratory, engineering, or scientific computing environments.

  • Experience preparing or maintaining DoD RMF authorization packages and using eMASS or a similar governance, risk, and compliance platform.

  • Experience implementing or validating DISA STIGs and supporting cybersecurity assessments, inspections, audits, or authorization activities.

  • Relevant cybersecurity certification such as CompTIA Security+, CySA+, ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC), CISSP, or another applicable certification.

Salary Range - $90,000 - $110,000

SMS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

title: Sr Director, Professional Services
description:
Job Summary

As Senior Director, EMEA Professional Services, you will lead NetApp’s EMEA Professional Services business with ownership of strategy, execution, and financial outcomes for a $100M+ services portfolio. Reporting to the VP/GM of Professional Services, you will lead an organization of over 150 professionals across the region. You will build on the strong foundation established in recent years and accelerate the shift to a services-led, outcome-led engagement model—expanding fee-based consulting and advisory that creates measurable customer outcomes, engages earlier in the lifecycle to shape solution direction, and drives profitable growth through increased attach and pull-through. The ideal candidate brings a consulting-led approach and strong commercial acumen to shape demand, quantify value, and convert executive advisory into funded engagements.

Context & Opportunity:

  • Worldwide Professional Services has invested in global delivery capabilities, harmonized sales and delivery processes, and expanded the use of a Global Services Center model.
  • In EMEA, Professional Services continues to evolve toward a consultative, outcome-led services model in close partnership with field sales.
  • EMEA Managed Services is an established, growing part of the portfolio, complementing project-based and advisory services.
  • The next phase is to scale a services-led consulting engine that engages earlier in the customer lifecycle to shape strategy, influence outcomes, and accelerate value realization.

Job Requirements

  • Own and lead the EMEA Professional Services business, including strategy, execution, and operating cadence to deliver profitable growth across bookings, revenue, and margin.
  • Scale fee-based consulting and advisory services that engage before product decisions—shaping customer vision, accelerating adoption, and driving measurable outcomes.
  • Partner with EMEA Sales and Solutions Engineering leadership to build services pipeline, create repeatable plays, and increase attach and pull-through through outcome-led services.
  • Develop and evolve the services portfolio (offer definition, packaging, pricing, and value messaging) to reduce reliance on free/presales work and low-value, product-tied attached services.
  • Lead a distributed organization of leaders, consultants, and delivery teams; coach talent, build succession, and foster a high-performance, inclusive culture.
  • Ensure high-quality, predictable delivery through standardized methods, governance, and risk management; improve utilization, project performance, and customer satisfaction.
  • Optimize the operating model across local delivery, partners, and global delivery centers; continuously improve processes and productivity.
  • Lead executive discovery and advisory plays to define roadmaps, build value cases, and convert strategy discussions into funded, fee-based consulting that drives attach and pull-through.
  • Represent Professional Services as a senior executive in key customer and partner engagements, including strategic account planning and executive briefings.
  • Drive alignment with Worldwide Professional Services, Portfolio, and Operations teams to scale best practices and implement business improvements.

Required Qualifications

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership in Professional Services, Consulting, and/or Managed Services within enterprise technology (hybrid cloud, storage, data management, security, automation).
  • Proven experience owning and growing a services P&L, including bookings, revenue recognition, margin, and cost management.
  • Demonstrated success building and scaling fee-based consulting and advisory offerings and influencing customers at executive level.
  • Strong partnership model with field sales: ability to build pipeline, establish services-led plays, and drive predictable commercial outcomes.
  • Experience leading consulting and transformation engagements, including executive discovery, roadmap development, and driving adoption/value realization.
  • Proven consultative selling to build pipeline and close fee-based advisory/consulting: shaping services-led plays, developing proposals/SOWs, and articulating ROI/value in partnership with Sales.
  • Experience leading large, geographically distributed organizations (including senior leaders) and operating effectively in a matrixed, global environment.
  • Excellent executive communication, negotiation, and customer-facing leadership skills.
  • Strong operational discipline: forecasting, governance, delivery quality, risk management, and continuous improvement.
  • Comfort working across partners and global delivery centers to scale capacity and standardize delivery.

At NetApp, we embrace a hybrid working environment designed to strengthen connection, collaboration, and culture for all employees. This means that most roles will have some level of in-office and/or in-person expectations, which will be shared during the recruitment process.
